extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 optical marker-based motion capture datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using SMPL body model parameters, including pose, shape, soft-tissue motion, and articulated hands when available. The dataset contains 42 hours of mocap data, 346 subjects, and 11,451 motions.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood; Nima Ghorbani; Nikolaus F. Troje; Gerard Pons-Moll; Michael J. Black
extraction.citeAs: Mahmood, Naureen, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, and Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by unifying 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets into a common SMPL-based representation using MoSh++. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet, several others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors, and marker data were mapped into common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. The paper also describes collection of a new SSM dataset using an OptiTrack motion capture system synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system; subjects wore minimal clothing and were fitted with reflective markers placed directly on the skin wherever possible.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. The method adjusts the pose prior weight as a function of the number of missing markers in a frame.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are archival optical marker-based human motion capture datasets with varying marker sets ranging from 37 to 91 markers, plus the newly collected SSM dataset containing synchronized marker-based mocap and 4D body scans. Source datasets include ACCAD, BioMotion Lab, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ maps sparse marker data from different source datasets into a unified SMPL representation. Each frame includes SMPL 3D shape parameters, DMPL soft-tissue coefficients, and full SMPL pose parameters including hand articulations. The authors manually inspected results and either corrected or held out problems caused by mocap issues such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The source datasets used varying marker sets and laboratory-specific procedures. MoSh++ fits a body model to sparse markers in two stages: first estimating subject shape and latent marker locations from randomly chosen frames, then estimating per-frame pose and soft-tissue dynamics. For SSM collection, subjects wore minimal clothing to avoid artifacts due to sliding cloth, and markers were placed directly on the skin wherever possible. For evaluation, the authors also used a standard 46-marker subset of the 67-marker SSM setup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is not described as having human semantic labels; instead, marker data are converted into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters using the MoSh++ fitting procedure. The paper explicitly notes inherent mocap problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers, and states that the authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually inspected the converted results and either corrected or held out problems due to swapped and mislabeled markers. For evaluation and hyperparameter tuning, they used scan-to-model distances on the SSM dataset and separated sequences into training, validation, and testing sets.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state that they will continue to expand the dataset, will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by them and the community, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape; hand articulation; motion capture markers placed on the body; 3D body scans in the SSM dataset. The paper also states that SSM consists of three subjects with varying body shapes, and two of the three subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable new applications that require large amounts of training data for animation and computer vision, and to generate synthetic training data for computer vision tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Existing mocap datasets are described as often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions. The source datasets in AMASS vary in format, marker sets, and laboratory-specific procedures. The SSM dataset used for tuning and evaluation consists of only three subjects with varying body shapes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Inherent mocap problems include swapped, mislabeled, and occluded markers. Missing markers can lead to unreliable and implausible poses. Hand articulation evaluation lacks ground-truth data. The current runtime of MoSh++ is not real-time. The SSM dataset used for evaluation contains only three subjects. The paper also notes that source datasets vary in marker sets and procedures.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for machine learning applications in animation and computer vision, including generating training data for deep learning, visualization, and synthetic training for computer vision tasks. Each frame provides pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters; users interested only in pose can ignore body shape and soft tissue deformations, and users can normalize bodies to the same shape if desired.
